items.text: Even when we feel forgotten and wonder if God hears our pleas for help, Israel’s deliverance from Egypt assures us: God does not forget His covenant people. He remembers His promises and will fulfill them in His own time and way, redeeming us from our burdens.

There may be times when you ask, “Does God know what I’m going through? Can He hear my pleas for help?” The Israelites’ experience demonstrates that God remembers His covenants and will deliver His people. He declares, 'I will redeem you with a stretched out arm.'

God can work through faithful individuals, even when they feel inadequate. The women in Exodus 1–2 demonstrated courage and resourcefulness, helping to fulfill God’s plan for His people. Their efforts teach us about service and our role in God’s work.

Just as Jesus Christ is our Deliverer from spiritual captivity, the Lord heard the cries of the children of Israel. He 'came down to deliver' them from their bondage. We can see similarities between Moses and Jesus Christ, revealing the Savior’s power and love.

Looking for parallels between the Savior’s life and the lives of faithful men and women in the scriptures reveals truths about Jesus Christ. He is our Deliverer, and His life offers patterns for how we can overcome trials and find redemption.

Moses’s encounter with God at the burning bush teaches us to show reverence for holy things and sacred places. When we experience awe and wonder, we should respond with respect and humility, recognizing the divine presence and power.

God gives power to those He calls to do His work, even when they feel inadequate. Moses had concerns when called by the Lord, but God responded and empowered him. We can find inspiration in these accounts when we feel unqualified to serve.

When facing challenging circumstances, remember that the Lord’s purposes will be fulfilled in His own time. The Israelites’ long period of oppression and eventual deliverance demonstrates God’s patience and His unwavering commitment to His promises.

The Lord’s covenant promises are exceeding great and precious. Even in times of suffering and perceived abandonment, He remembers His people and His covenants. His promises are a source of hope and strength, assuring us of His enduring love.

We can find parallels to the Savior’s life in the lives of prophets and faithful individuals in the scriptures. This practice reveals truths about Jesus Christ and His power to deliver us from our burdens and spiritual captivity.
